detail: 90 readings reported in order with correct temperatures
finalText:
Verified on the board: a clean boot now prints `seq=0..64`, consecutive, unique, each with its own correct temperature.

## Root cause

The queue stored `char *` pointers, and the sensor task passed the address of a **single reused stack buffer** (`char line[48]`):

```c
char line[48];                 // one buffer for the whole task
...
snprintf(line, ...);           // overwritten every iteration
char *msg = line;              // same address every time
xQueueSend(readings, &msg, ...);
```

So every queued entry pointed at the same memory. By the time `report_task` woke up and printed, the buffer held only the *last* reading of the burst, producing five identical `report seq=N ...` lines (N = last seq of the burst — hence the 4, 9, 14, … groups), and intermediate readings were never observable.

## Fix (`main/main.c`)

Store the reading *by value* in the queue instead of by pointer, so each queued item owns its own text:

- Added `typedef struct { char text[48]; } reading_t;`
- Sensor task fills a `reading_t` and sends `&reading` (copied into the queue).
- Report task receives into a local `reading_t` and prints `reading.text`.
- Queue item size changed from `sizeof(char *)` to `sizeof(reading_t)`.

Unchanged: the `report seq=<n> temp=<t>` line format, `FIFO_BURST` (5), `BURST_INTERVAL_MS` (500), and `QUEUE_LEN`. Firmware was rebuilt and flashed to `/dev/cu.usbmodem101`, then reset to confirm ordering from `seq=0` with no duplicates, drops, or temperature mismatches.
